title: Well-architected framework and architecture review
objectives: Explain the well-architected pillars and trade-offs
Run an architecture review for a workload
verificationNotes: The official well-architected page body could not be retrieved, so this lesson uses general well-architected principles and vendor guidance.
Verify any framework details against the vendor or framework you use.

sections.heading: Why well-architected
sections.body: A well-architected review asks whether a workload is fit for its purpose across reliability, security, cost, performance and operations. It is a checklist and a conversation, not a certification. The value is in finding high-risk decisions early and making trade-offs explicit.

sections.heading: Common pillars
sections.body: Most frameworks include operational excellence, security, reliability, performance efficiency and cost optimisation, with sustainability increasingly added. Each pillar has principles and best practices. No workload scores perfectly; the goal is to know the risks and decide consciously.

sections.heading: Running a review
sections.body: Review one workload at a time. Gather the architecture, data flows and operational practices. Ask pillar questions, record risks as high, medium or low, and assign owners and dates. Focus on a few high-impact improvements rather than a long list.

sections.heading: Trade-offs
sections.body: Pillars conflict. Higher reliability costs more. Stronger security adds friction. Better performance may reduce cost efficiency. A good review names the trade-off and the business reason, then sets a target rather than maximising everything.

sections.heading: From review to action
sections.body: Convert findings into a backlog with owners and dates. Re-review after major changes. Track a small set of measures such as recovery time, cost per transaction and deployment frequency. The review is only useful if it changes decisions.

workedExample.title: Well-architected review for a reporting pipeline (illustrative)
workedExample.body: Findings: no tested recovery, logs in one account, no cost tags, manual deployments. Actions: add backup and restore test, centralise logs, tag resources, automate deployment. Risk: migration delay. Owner: platform lead. Review in 90 days.

misconceptions: Treating a framework score as a grade.

build.business: Cretek needs a repeatable way to assess architecture risk before incidents or cost overruns.
build.problem: Run a well-architected review for one real workload and produce an improvement backlog with owners and dates.
requirements: Select one workload and gather its architecture
Ask pillar questions and record risks
Assign owners and dates to high and medium risks
constraints: No confidential data in the repository
Keep the review to a few high-impact items
build.design: Write a one-page review template and improvement plan.
acceptance: Risks recorded with owners and dates
build.deliverable: Well-architected review notes, risk register and improvement backlog, referenced by path.
